ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: On the right side of the figure is a capacitor C, the voltage u is marked on the left side, with polarity “+” at the upper end and “-” at the lower end. The arrow of current i points to the right on the upper wire, indicating that the current enters the capacitor from the upper end, consistent with the positive terminal of voltage u, satisfying the passive sign convention. Reasoning: It is known that C = 1 μF = 1×10^-6 F, u(t) = 500 sin(1000t) V. The capacitor current relationship is i = C du/dt. Differentiate the voltage: du/dt = 500×1000 cos(1000t) = 500000 cos(1000t) V/s. Therefore i = 1×10^-6 × 500000 cos(1000t) = 0.5 cos(1000t) A. Also cos(1000t) = sin(1000t + 90°), so i = 0.5 sin(1000t + 90°) A.
